answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-). EBER negative; CD5 negative; no low-grade (follicular) component.
answer.stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage IA: a single nodal region (right cervical levels II-III, contiguous), with no B symptoms (denies fevers, night sweats and weight loss). Non-bulky: largest node 3.1 cm, well below the 7.5 cm threshold used in limited-stage trials. No extranodal, splenic or marrow disease on PET-CT. Bone marrow biopsy is not needed because PET-CT shows homogeneous marrow activity without focal uptake.
answer.biology: Neither double-expressor nor double-hit. MYC 15% and BCL2 30% by IHC are below the 40%/50% thresholds. FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. Ki-67 ~55%.
answer.prognosis: IPI 0 of 5, low risk: age 45 (<=60), LDH normal (190 U/L), ECOG 0, stage I, no extranodal sites. CNS-IPI 0, low risk. Age 18-60, IPI 0 and maximum diameter <7.5 cm meet the FLYER trial eligibility criteria; expected 3-year progression-free survival is about 95%.
answer.first_line_treatment: Curative-intent immunochemotherapy. Recommend R-CHOP for 4 cycles followed by 2 additional doses of rituximab, without radiotherapy (FLYER regimen: 4 cycles of R-CHOP plus 2 rituximab was non-inferior to 6 cycles in young patients with IPI 0 and non-bulky disease, with less toxicity). Six cycles of R-CHOP are not needed. Omitting radiotherapy also respects her wish to avoid neck radiation and spares the thyroid and salivary glands, a real concern given her sister's radiation-induced hypothyroidism. Acceptable alternatives: R-CHOP x3 followed by involved-site radiotherapy (ISRT), or a PET-adapted approach after 4 cycles (S1001). Pola-R-CHP is not indicated: POLARIX enrolled IPI 2-5 only. DA-EPOCH-R is not indicated.
answer.cns_risk: Low CNS-relapse risk: CNS-IPI 0 and no high-risk extranodal sites (kidney, adrenal, testis, breast, uterus). CNS prophylaxis is not indicated, and no MRI brain or lumbar puncture is required without neurological symptoms.
answer.response_assessment: Interim PET-CT after 4 cycles of R-CHOP, before the two rituximab doses: Deauville 1-3 supports completing the plan without radiotherapy; Deauville 4-5 should prompt biopsy or consolidative ISRT rather than proceeding as planned. End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last dose, read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale; Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response. Routine surveillance imaging is not needed after a complete metabolic response.
answer.pretreatment_workup: A pregnancy test (serum or urine hCG) is required before cycle 1; none is documented in this premenopausal woman (LMP 2026-08-28, day 21 of her cycle). Hepatitis B serology done: HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive (anti-HBs reactive from vaccination), so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed before rituximab. HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echo LVEF 63%, so anthracycline is permitted. Organ function and blood counts normal.
answer.supportive_care: Stop the combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) now: estrogen-containing contraception is contraindicated in migraine with aura because of ischemic stroke risk, and it adds venous thromboembolism risk on top of active lymphoma and chemotherapy. She still needs effective non-estrogen contraception throughout treatment and for at least 12 months after: a levonorgestrel or copper IUD is preferred (a levonorgestrel IUD also limits heavy bleeding during thrombocytopenia), or an etonogestrel implant or progestin-only pill; arrange gynecology referral and use condoms until it is in place. Fertility counselling: 4 cycles of R-CHOP carry low gonadotoxicity at age 45 and most women resume menses, but age-related fertility decline matters; offer referral to reproductive medicine before starting since she is undecided about another pregnancy, without delaying treatment. Tumor lysis risk is low (normal LDH, uric acid and renal function); oral hydration, allopurinol optional. Primary G-CSF is not routinely required at age 45 with no risk factors, but reassess after cycle 1. Antiemetics per regimen; avoid codeine (intolerance). Rituximab infusion-reaction precautions.
answer.fitness_and_goals: Fit: ECOG 0 with no limiting comorbidity, so curative-intent therapy is appropriate with a high cure probability. Her goals are cure, continuing to work as a teacher with minimal time off, and avoiding neck radiation; the 4 x R-CHOP + 2 x rituximab plan without radiotherapy matches all three, and schedules can place infusions late in the week so she can keep teaching. Shared decision-making about the radiotherapy-containing alternative documented.
